findings.title: Post-phase authority failure skips both terminal journaling and rollback
findings.observation: advance always revalidates before persistence. If an active phase succeeds but post-phase revalidation fails, the catch path calls advance(FAILED), repeats the same failing revalidation, and exits before FAILED, ROLLING_BACK or rollback. The CLI then releases the lock while the persisted attempt remains at the previous forward state. Active backup/restore child pipelines also lack a controller deadline, so a blocked oracle never reaches the designed four-hour terminal boundary.
findings.trigger: Let a valid phase complete after its envelope expires or mutate the bound request/runtime between the pre-phase and pre-append checks; an unbounded backup/restore child can produce the same stranded state after operator termination.
findings.impact: A migration, candidate app/Caddy, backup or restore side effect can exist without a matching journal append, failure record, ingress disable or rollback. Clean-lock re-entry rejects the persisted forward state, leaving an ambiguous partially mutated deployment contrary to AC 11 and the approved recovery contract.

evidence.description: Exact-head pure local counterexample produced one external phase call, three revalidations and zero rollback calls before returning AUTHORITY_EXPIRED_AFTER_PHASE.
Success advance and catch-path FAILED advance both invoke the same revalidate before persistence.
The CLI always releases the target lock in finally even when runDeployment exits with the prior forward record unchanged.
The approved design requires terminal failure/rollback and a four-hour attempt maximum; backup and restore spawn pipelines have no timeout.

findings.remediation: Separate authorization for new forward mutations from safety recovery. Guarantee a durable terminal/rollback path for any post-operation failure even when forward revalidation fails, without authorizing another forward phase. Enforce the attempt deadline and bounded child termination, keep exact call ordering, and leave a recoverable terminal/interrupted record rather than a clean-lock forward state.
findings.verification: At every phase boundary, fail expiry/request/runtime revalidation after the oracle returns and assert the external call count, exactly one ingress-disable/rollback, durable FAILED -> ROLLING_BACK -> terminal transitions, and no later phase. A hung backup/restore process must terminate at the deadline and follow the same recovery path.

findings.title: Restore faults leave the isolated database environment running
findings.observation: RESTORE_ENVIRONMENT creates the isolated PostgreSQL project, but compose down --volumes exists only near the end of the successful RESTORE case. No finally or stale-recovery cleanup owns that project. Generic rollback only operates on the production app/caddy project and cannot remove the isolated resources.
findings.trigger: Fail or crash after isolated PostgreSQL creation and before successful down/verification, including destination inspection, decrypt/import, migration, app readiness, demo replay, migration proof or production reinspection.
findings.impact: The restored database container, loopback app and persistent volume can remain after failure, retaining restored synthetic data, consuming disk/ports, blocking deterministic reuse and violating the explicit restore-failure cleanup contract while the deployment is marked failed.

evidence.description: Restore project creation precedes many throwing operations; the only removal is success-path compose down --volumes.
Active rollback delegates to production application rollback, whose adapter does not know the restore project.
The every-phase fault test mocks abstract oracles and asserts only one generic rollback call; it never instantiates host operations or asserts restore container/volume cleanup.
Requirements explicitly require failed restore smoke to clean only the isolated temporary environment while preserving backup and production data.

findings.remediation: Own the exact restore project/container/volume lifecycle across success, handled failure and stale-lock recovery. Clean only resources matching the persisted isolated identity, record cleanup outcome separately from production rollback, and preserve production plus backup evidence.
findings.verification: Inject a fault at every operation from restore environment creation through production reinspection, plus a crash/recovery case; each must leave zero matching restore containers/volumes, preserve production byte-identity and backup files, and record cleanup before terminalization.

required_actions.action: Replace caller-authored external smoke PASS with active authority-bound observation and certificate validation.
Replace bundle-backed production oracles with active live deployment operations and explicit bounded interruption/resume.
Bind pg_restore to the exact inspected isolated container and independently observe production identity.
Configure and prove required CSP plus exact same-host HTTPS redirect semantics.
Make post-operation authority/deadline failures terminal and rollback-safe without enabling new forward mutation.
Clean exact isolated restore resources on every failure and crash-recovery path.
